notes.title: Small Update v0.8.9.4
notes.notes:
[h1]Game Master Engine Update v0.8.9.4[/h1]

Greetings, GMs!
This update brings exciting tools, enhancements, and experimental features designed to speed up your workflow and expand what's possible in your worlds. Here’s everything included in v0.8.9.4:

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[b]New Mouse Look Mode (Press M):[/b]
Navigate your scene with greater control using the new free-look mode. Press M to toggle it on or off, giving you full 360° camera movement for easier editing and inspection.

[b]New Brush Tool (Press B):[/b]
The new Brush Tool allows you to select props—like trees, rocks, or debris—and "paint" them across your map. It randomly places the selected assets within your brush radius, making it fast and easy to populate large areas like forests or ruins.

[b]World Manager Tag Search:[/b]
Easily search for pins by tags in the World Manager. Whether you're looking for quest markers or custom labels, this new search option helps you stay organized in complex maps.

[b]Select All Button (Gizmo UI):[/b]
A new Select All button has been added to the Gizmo UI. With one click, you can now select every instance of your currently selected prop across the entire map—ideal for mass edits or quick replacements.

[h2]Experimental Features (GM Edition Only)[/h2]
[b]Shop Marker (Experimental):[/b]
Early groundwork for shop zones has been added. This marker will eventually allow players to interact with designated areas as shops, giving you more in-world gameplay tools.

[b]Dungeon Spawner (Experimental):[/b]
While this tool is currently called “Dungeon Spawner,” it is already capable of much more. Use it to quickly generate environments like dungeons, forests, villages, and swamps. It’s in early stages but offers a glimpse of powerful procedural tools coming soon.

[h3]The following images are examples of what the [b]Dungeon Spawner[/b] is capable of creating.[/h3]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/B4rhJXt.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jocZGiK.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/c5pj2KB.png[/img]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[b]Improved Collision in Elven Ruins:[/b]
Several props in the Elven Ruins asset set had inaccurate collision settings—these have now been corrected for smoother gameplay.

[b]Trash Bin Enhancements:[/b]
The World Manager’s Trash Bin received backend improvements for better reliability when recovering deleted objects.

notes.title: Small Patch v0.8.9.2
notes.notes:
[h1]Game Master Engine Update v0.8.9.2[/h1]

Dear GMs,
We are excited to announce the latest update for Game Master Engine, featuring key performance enhancements and a completely redesigned initiative tracker. This update focuses on improving your experience, from smoother gameplay to better tools for managing encounters. Here’s a closer look at the changes:

[h2]Performance Improvements[/h2]
FPS Enhancements & Model Optimization:
We’ve introduced a variety of general improvements to boost FPS in both standard and complex use cases. Numerous models have been optimized to leverage Unreal Engine 5’s Nanite technology, enabling you to place more objects on screen with greater performance. Whether you’re constructing detailed maps or using complex props, you should experience smoother and more responsive gameplay.

[h3]Optimized Animated Props:[/h3]
We’ve addressed a performance issue affecting certain animated props, particularly animals like goats, which were previously causing performance drops. These animations have been optimized to ensure better performance when using animated elements, making your worlds more efficient and dynamic.

[h2]New Features[/h2]
Revamped Initiative Tracker:
The old initiative tracker has been completely replaced with a new, more efficient system, accessible under the "Combat" tab for GMs. This updated tracker is designed to simplify encounter management while offering greater flexibility.

[h3]Key Features Include:[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Mini Dashboard Integration:[/b] Easily add minis to the initiative tracker through the "Mini Dashboard", streamlining the setup of encounters.
[/list]
[list]
[*] [b]Round and Turn Tracking:[/b] The system automatically tracks rounds and turns, providing an intuitive way to follow combat progression.
[/list]
[list]
[*] [b]Turn Highlighting:[/b] Keep track of whose turn it is with turn highlighting, reducing confusion during encounters.
[/list]
[list]
[*] [b]Easy Sorting by Initiative:[/b] While participants are not automatically sorted by initiative, a simple "Sort" button allows you to organize participants in order with minimal effort.
[/list]

This is just the first phase of our initiative tracker’s redesign, and we have more improvements on the way, including:

[list]
[*] [b]Multiple Encounters per Map:[/b] Manage several encounters on a single map, allowing for more complex combat scenarios.
[/list]
[list]
[*] [b]Status Effects and Concentration Tracking:[/b] Easily track active status effects and concentration spells for more strategic combat management.
[/list]
[list]
[*] [b]Multiplayer Integration:[/b] In an upcoming update, all players will be able to view the turn order, keeping everyone on the same page during multiplayer sessions.
[/list]

Thank you for your continued support of Game Master Engine. We are dedicated to enhancing your experience and look forward to your feedback as we continue to improve the platform.

Best regards,
The Game Master Engine Team

notes.title: Small Patch v0.8.9.1.1
notes.notes:
[h2]Features:[/h2]

This update is more focused on bug fixes, but we’ve added a few neat features to enhance your experience:

[b]Report a Bug Button:[/b] A new “Report a Bug” button has been added to the help menu, making it easier to report any issues you encounter.

[b]Request A Feature:[/b] You can now access a form in the help menu to request a feature or tutorial in GME. We’re eager to hear your suggestions and improve the platform based on your feedback.

[b]Campaign Map Sorting:[/b] Players can once again sort their maps into campaigns, which are now correctly displayed.

[b]Revamped Mini Radial Menu:[/b] The Mini radial menu has been replaced with a cleaner and more intuitive interface.

[b]Custom Object Menu:[/b] The “Simple Shape” tool is now called “Custom Object” and has received a new, streamlined menu.

[b]Updated Keybinds Section:[/b] The keybinds section has been refreshed for easier navigation and customization.

[h2]Major Bugfixes:[/h2]

[b]Shader Model Issue:[/b] A bug that prevented many graphics cards from using the correct shader model, resulting in poor performance even on high-end machines, has been fixed. The correct shader models are now in use.

[b]Floor Mat Flickering:[/b] A bug causing intense flickering on the floor mat for some systems, particularly those with AMD graphics cards, has been resolved.

[b]Dice Rolling Error:[/b] An error in the dice rolling system that resulted in absurdly high numbers due to a conversion issue has been corrected. No more accidental 1d20 minus 700 million rolls!

[b]Ruler Deletion:[/b] A bug that prevented rulers from being deleted correctly by players has been fixed. Ruler deletion now works as intended.

[b]Hidden Layers Issue:[/b] An issue where hidden layers would not reappear correctly after a map was saved and reloaded has been addressed. Hidden layers now function properly.

[b]Grouping Box Stability:[/b] The grouping box is now more stable and able to grab objects as expected after fixing a related bug.

[b]Mini Right Click Menu:[/b] Fixed a bug that caused the new right-click menu for minis to become invisible after a map transition.

[b]Quick Access Minis:[/b] Fixed a bug that prevented minis added to the world from your saved quick access from being correctly added to the "Mini Dashboard."

[h2]Minor Bugfixes:[/h2]

[b]Multiplayer Exit:[/b] A bug that prevented players from reliably leaving multiplayer games, forcing them to quit the game entirely, has been fixed.

[b]Grid on Invisible Objects:[/b] An issue where the grid would appear on invisible or deleted objects has been resolved.

[b]Cone Ruler Direction:[/b] Fixed a bug where the cone rulers would face the wrong direction when spawned, causing them to flip around when grabbed.

[b]Line Ruler Text:[/b] Fixed a bug where the text for a line ruler would not follow it around and would instead remain floating at its original spawn point.

[b]Ghost Cat On Horse:[/b] Fixed a mysterious bug where a cat would randomly spawn with one of the horse models. We're not sure how it got there, but after some gentle persuasion and a bit of ghostbusting, the cat has moved on to greener pastures. Farewell, brave steed rider!

notes.title: Patch notes 0.8.5.1
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.postimg.cc/VkhSDFG5/Elven-Gold2.png[/img]

[b]Mini Importing:[/b]

- The empty mini plate can now also be used to import custom miniatures.

- Imported Minis are now loaded more reliably, as some people were experiencing issues with them when reloading their maps.

- Imported Minis can now be saved to the mini quick access and retrieved correctly.

[b]Flexible Grid:[/b]

- The new flexible grid system replaces the old system. This grid appears on tiles and all landscape objects (like rocks and such) when turned on, and follows the terrain if that terrain was built either out of objects or from tiles. The feature can be turned off and on by each player individually.

- A bug was removed where deleting such an object would leave a residue grid in the world.

- To update the grid after changing objects in other ways (moving, scaling, etc.), the grid needs to be turned off and on again (for performance reasons, instead of updating the grid in real time)

- The Simple Shape object’s default behavior is now to receive a grid when the grid is turned on.

- To change if an object receives a grid or not, you can select it and press Shift-G, then turn the grid off and on again.

- Many objects have been set to automatically receive a grid in this update.

[b]Other Bugfixes:[/b]

- Some objects in the “Exterior / Elven Castle” Set had no collision and therefore could not be manipulated properly. This has been fixed.

- There was a bug with objects attached to grouping boxes that had been rotated after attachment. This has been fixed.

- You can control-click a mini to move/scale/rotate it with the gizmo, but there was a bug with this where the gizmo would interfere with moving the mini normally. This was fixed.

- Deleted Line Rulers were not removed for players correctly, but are now.

- Rotating the Camera with the left and right arrow keys was jittery, and is now smooth.

Additions to the Game:

12 new pre-colored minis have been added to the game.

notes.title: Game Master Engine Update 0.8.5
notes.notes:
[h1]Game Master Engine Update 0.8.5 Patch Notes[/h1]

We’re excited to announce that version 0.8.5 of Game Master Engine has just dropped! This update brings a host of quality-of-life improvements, new features, and over 600 new sci-fi props as we prepare for the next major update!

[img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/950513097808965662/1208208199446954066/SciFiCityNight.png?ex=6659c252&is=665870d2&hm=3b2619f34067ddce4c4c5dd46bd8d80582c4f2b4840d2f57e1482e51e2f63e08&=&format=webp&quality=lossless&width=1080&height=607[/img]

[h2]New Features:[/h2]

[h3]Space Sky Function[/h3]
[b]Description:[/b] A new addition to the atmosphere settings, the Space Sky function allows you to activate a space mode. Found at the bottom of the atmosphere settings.

[b]Use Case:[/b] This is not only useful for science fiction adventures but also perfect for creating eerie dungeons and otherworldly scenes.

[h3]Improved Import/Export[/h3]
[b]Description:[/b] Access the object functions window with CTRL-F, where the Import/Export function has seen significant improvements.

[b]Enhancements:[/b] Recolored objects can now be imported correctly, making it easier to transfer your custom designs.

[h3]Spline Tool[/h3]
[b]Description:[/b] By pressing N on an object, you can activate the spline feature, allowing for the deformation and extension of objects.

[b]Applications: [/b] Ideal for creating dynamic walls, winding rivers, and sprawling roads.

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/950513097808965662/1245840942808830083/image.png?ex=665a374b&is=6658e5cb&hm=f9142f175d0938383ad8b5d12715a85867ce71416967d8af7613a19ba7a5c70d&[/img]

[h3]Advanced Graphics Settings[/h3]
[b]Description:[/b] A new set of graphics options is now available to fine-tune your gaming experience.

[b]Purpose:[/b] These settings aim to help players optimize performance and visuals, getting the most out of their hardware.

[h2]Bugfixes:[/h2]

[h3]Elven Town Objects[/h3]
[b]Issue:[/b] Some objects in the “elven town” set lacked collision, rendering them unclickable.

[b]Resolution:[/b] This has been fixed to ensure all objects are interactive.

[h3]Grouping Box[/h3]
[b]Issue:[/b] The ungroup button was redundant.

[b]Resolution:[/b] The ungroup button has been removed. To ungroup objects, simply delete the grouping box.

[h3]Trash Bin Frequency[/h3]
[b]Issue:[/b] The Trash bin was deleting its contents too frequently.

[b]Resolution:[/b] Now, it only deletes contents upon loading a map or when emptied manually.

[h3]Grouping/Selection Box[/h3]
[b]Issue: [/b]The grouping/selection box would sometimes collide with the camera, causing flickering.

[b]Resolution:[/b] This issue has been resolved for a smoother experience.

[h3]Lens Flare Effect[/h3]
[b]Issue:[/b] The lens flare effect was overly strong, causing lighting artifacts.

[b]Resolution:[/b] The effect has been toned down for a more realistic appearance.

[h3]Empty Mini Object[/h3]
[b]Issue:[/b] The “empty mini” object couldn’t import custom minis, unlike other minis.

[b]Resolution:[/b] This has been corrected to allow custom mini imports.

[h2]Outlook:[/h2]

We’re currently reworking the UI to be more intuitive, sleek, and modern. Additionally, we’re transitioning to Unreal Engine 5 as our base engine. A functional version is already in the works, but we’re refining the details. Stay tuned for more updates!

Thank you for your continued support and feedback. Happy gaming!

notes.title: Anniversary Update v0.8.4.1
notes.notes:
[h1]New Features [/h1]


[h2]Simple Shape Texture (GM Version Only)[/h2]


You can also use simple shapes to force a texture from one object to another object. This does work with every object. It’s an advanced feature, and some textures might not fit on every object, but it unlocks a whole new world of creativity!


We added this feature to remove all restrictions on coloring options.
In contrast to the custom model importing, you can also use this as often as you want on a given map, since it does not impact performance.



[h2]Prop Importing with Simple Shapes[/h2]

You can now also use Simple Shapes to import your own Props in the FBX, OBJ or STL format. To do so, control-click a simple shape and hit the little red button at the top, then follow the instructions. Keep in mind that players have to have the model too in order for this to show up, so this is rather for private campaigns. This is analogue to the mini importing function that was introduced in the last version.


This feature allows map makers to be more creative and less bound by what the game already brings to the table. However, this feature should not be used excessively: If something can be solved without importing custom props, it should. With this feature we also want to show you that the game we want to create is open for your input - we want to make a game engine, not a marketplace for asset packs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39242012/ef3597c3a7b6a2641f3def4696c19f2dba186c74.png[/img]
[i]Importing a Palm tree that I made in 3 minutes in Blender - I’m sure you can do it better! ;)[/i]


[h2]Sound Objects[/h2]


You can use a Sound object to either play sounds that come with the game or import your sounds. This is meant for long-playing sounds such as music and soundscapes. Control-right-click the sound object to see your options. 


We added this feature to allow for greater immersion and 3D control of sounds in your campaign. For many DM’s, sound is an essential part of their gaming, and this tool allows a lot of control and integration of sound into the 3D environment.


[h2]Forced Perspective for Camera Nodes[/h2]

The Camera Nodes have been massively improved with the ability to bind your players to them with forcing the camera’s perspective for them. You can even move the camera around with the players attached to it, thereby moving their vision around. 
Also, you can now jump to the camera’s position with the “Preview Camera” function, though this does not root you to it (neither does it rotate your vision).


The camera nodes where an older function of GME that was never really efficient, but nevertheless was popular with a lot of users, so we decided to improve it. This also allows for cinematic sequences, self-made loading-screens, game pauses and so on.


[h2]Spline Dragging[/h2]


You can hit N on an object to drag a spline from it. This will make a new version of the object that stretches following your mouse. This is useful for walls, rivers, and roads, but also to deform props in a way that was not possible before. If the object is facing the wrong way, you can use Alt-N or Ctrl-N instead to find the right alignment.


We added this feature because there was a great need especially for roads, and no easy way to create them. Now you can!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39242012/fb2b2372e7caa07d7d95ffd544c4d0dfb5f71747.png[/img]
[i]There are three splines in this image: the rune wall, the pipeline, and the wooden logs. You can drag a spline from any object in Game Master Engine.[/i]


[h2]Improved Import / Export[/h2]

By Pressing CTRL-F, you can bring up the Object Options window, where you can do a bunch of useful tricks to change large portions of your map at once. One particularly useful feature here is Import/Export. With this, you can export parts of your map or your whole map to a .txt file which you can easily share with others. These can then be imported into other existing maps - so you can take your friends castle and incorporate it in your map! The resulting text files are called “Schematics” and can be found in C:\GME Map Exports\Schematics (If you don’t have that folder, export a map and the game will create it for you). That’s also where other people’s files go!


We added this feature since it allows people to migrate constructions between maps and share them more easily with each other.


[h2]Angle Snapping[/h2]

While holding the I key (as in ice-cream) while placing an object, the object will try to snap to the angle of whatever it is on. This only works with Z-Snap activated. It also works for miniatures.


We added this feature to work in conjunction with Spline dragging. While Splines automatically have this behaviour, other objects did not, so we enabled this.


[h1]New Content[/h1]



[h2]Over 50 New Painted and Recolorable Minis[/h2]


Our awesome community has created a lot of recolorable versions of the minis that were in the game before. With their friendly permission, we included these into the game. Thank you! They come pre-colored, but using the paint-brush menu in the mini menu (right-click the mini) you can select which zone to repaint in which way. If you want more freedom than that still, you can recolor these minis using the simple shape.


We added this because the uncolored minis were always a weak point of GME. More minis are to come in the upcoming versions. We also host the weekly Mini Painting Saturday, where we meet to paint even more minis.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39242012/7650a1f2fa07a0edd24c5a5ebf04c93d2eff9328.png[/img]
[i]Finally the gelatinous wizard has found a town that is as accepting and friendly as himself! The two dragonborn children are the same base model.[/i]


[h2]Over 400 New Props of different genres[/h2]


We added many many props from different genres, for example Asian-Style, Arabian-Style, Snowlands, Steampunk (in Sci-Fi) and others. Have a look through the menus and see what’s new!


These were added to allow people to create more and more diverse maps. I would include a screenshot here, but it’s simply too much stuff to show in a screenshot. Just check it out in the game! :) 


[h2]One-Off-Effects (GM Version Only)[/h2]

You can find new one-off effects in the effects category. Players see those in your hand, even without placing them, but they are invisible as long as you hold shift. This is GM version only because it only makes sense in multiplayer, and you need the GM version to host games.
When you place the effect, it will instead turn into an explosion of its appropriate type (so fire turns into a fireball) and then vanish. If you don’t want such an explosion, just end with a right-click instead. Currently, only the GM can place these effects.


We added this feature because it provides a versatile and spell-independent way to create stunning effects in multiplayer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39242012/eb7e7dade35400a8e2237aad3f68b2e9401b880d.png[/img]
[i]The Magic Academy is a dangerous place indeed! The effect seen here is a one-off-effect that you can place, and then it will explode like here.[/i]


[h2]Placeable Smoke, Fog and Butterflies![/h2]


Also among the effects you can find Smoke and fog. The effects are very visible in the night and not so much in daytime. The butterflies are cute too!


We added this because it provides a great way to play with the feeling and lighting of a scene. Also we love butterflies. 


[h1]Feature Improvements[/h1]


[h2]Improved Dice Rolling[/h2]


With the new dice roller, you can now roll any combination of dice. You can roll these in 3D (Standard) or hold alt while clicking “roll” to directly roll them via random number generation (that is quicker and easier on the PC/Network).


We added this to improve the usability of GME as a Virtual Tabletop. We’re also working on more Macro options for the next feature Update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39242012/336a91eb66259452fde68a9d1409e43cb2b37c59.png[/img]
[i]I rolled poorly, so our adventurer survived the skeleton’s attack. Before, you could only roll one dice type at a time, now you can roll 11d10+3d6+5.[/i]


[h2]Improved First Person Camera[/h2]


The performance of the first person camera mode was drastically improved, especially in multiplayer. You can switch into first person camera by hitting CTRL-O, or by using a mini to switch into its first person view (via the round menu you get by right clicking the mini, then hitting the silhouette-shaped button).


The camera was a bit laggy at times in multiplayer before. This is now relieved.


[h2]Improved Mini Quick Access[/h2]


When saving a Mini to Quick access, it now saves up to 20 material changes and up to 10 attached objects right away in the quiver, so when you bring the Mini back at a later point, it will come with these objects attached to it. That means you can put a helmet and a shield on your rogue (click the helmet, hover the rogue, hit ctrl-g) to potentially turn them into a fighter. In principle, you can make your mini from props using the empty Mini plate in this way.


This improves the customizability of minis even further - because who doesn’t want their very own Mini creation?


[h2]Improved Lighting[/h2]


The lights in GME now look significantly better, and the distance fog is back, giving scenes a way more realistic look. Also, there are now overhauled placeable light sources, not only as point lights but also as spotlights. These come in different colors, but can be recolored to your liking if needed.


We added this to give you the ability to make your maps look more awesome. Light is a significant factor in presenting an arrangement.



[h2]Improved Atmosphere Settings[/h2]


You can now set a bunch of new options in the atmosphere settings, like cloud color and cloud height (move the clouds to the ground and tint them orange to get amazing sandstorms!) and other options like sky color. You can even set a day/night cycle!


We added this feature to give you more control over your scene, but also to enable the creation of maps that were impossible to make before. Want to fight the back of a dragon in the clouds? We have you covered!

Also, this is not an after-effect when taking a screenshot - You could play like this if you really really want to![/i]


[h1]Other things[/h1]


[h2]Video Tutorials available on Discord[/h2]

	Feel free to have a look, while we are working on overhauling the complete tutorial section for all the other topics as well :) 

[h2]Mini Painting Saturdays[/h2]

	Also on our discord, we meet with our community on Saturdays to paint some minis and chat about what’s going on, just having a good time.
	You are more than welcome to join us there :) 

[h2]Next up: Sci-Fi Update[/h2]

You’ve asked about it so much that we took it to heart. The next update will be on Sci-Fi of all kinds, from Grimdark to Solarpunk, while also
adding props for near future modernity and steampunk settings. ETA for this update is April 2024.

If you made it to here, thanks for your time, and enjoy the game!

notes.title: v0.8.4 New Tools Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Major Changes[/h1]

[h2]Tutorial Maps / Premade Maps:[/h2]

An extensive tutorial map has been added to guide new players through the basics of GME. It's accessible from the main menu or while loading a map in-game.
A new "premade" category is now available when you go to "load map", featuring 32 premade maps for quick and diverse gameplay options.

[h2]First Person View:[/h2]

First-person mode is finally here! Players can now switch to this mode by right-clicking on a mini they control and selecting the silhouette icon. Alternatively, pressing CTRL-O drops you into first-person view, and pressing it again returns you to free-flying mode.

[h2]Quick Measuring:[/h2]

Measure distances quickly by holding ALT and click-dragging from one point to another. You can also add waypoints to your measurement by clicking while holding ALT. When dragging a mini, tapping ALT allows for waypoint-based measurement too.

[h2]Colored Miniatures:[/h2]

The minis section now includes colored and recolorable miniatures. For those interested in contributing to this feature, join us on Discord—recolor minis by opening their radial menu and selecting the paintbrush icon.

[h2]Quick Grouping:[/h2]

Group objects easily by clicking on an object (A), hovering over another (B), and pressing CTRL-G. Object A will follow Object B when moved, and you can adjust its relative position.

[h2]Mini Quick Access Improvement:[/h2]

The Quick Access for minis now saves coloration, including for multi-colored minis. When you save a mini, all attached objects are also saved, allowing quick access to fully equipped minis.

[h2]Prop Trash Bin:[/h2]

Deleted objects are now moved to a trash bin, where they can be recovered until the map is saved. The trash bin is located in the top right corner of the screen in the World Manager.

[h1]Minor Changes[/h1]

[h2]Key Rebinding's:[/h2]

Customize your key bindings in-game using the keyboard button in the top right. A comprehensive overview of shortcuts is also available in this section.

[h2]Campaign Management:[/h2]

GME now automatically sorts maps into campaigns based on their names, streamlining map organization. The save menu provides options for saving maps as part of a campaign.

[h2]Selection Box & Grouping Box:[/h2]

Use G and left-click drag to create a selection box, or use the right mouse button for a grouping box. Follow on-screen instructions for these useful features.

[h2]Improved Snapping:[/h2]

The snapping system has been refined. With Grid-Snap turned on (Y key), objects snap into a 5-foot-grid. Grid-Snapping and Z-Snapping now work simultaneously.

[h2]New Ocean Options:[/h2]

Two new water styles are available in the ocean settings, complete with an underwater effect.

[h2]Scrolls, Books, Chests Interactivity:[/h2]

Books and chests can now be interacted with by right-clicking. Books update in real-time, and chests can be locked for player exploration.

[h2]Grid Object & Support Plane:[/h2]

New GM tool objects, including the "Grid Object" for displaying a 5-foot-grid and the "Support Plane Object" which is invisible to players but useful for placing flying characters or objects.

[h2]Open Maps Folder:[/h2]

Easily access your maps folder from the main menu or save/load window. Look for "premade__" maps which are automatically created for you.

[h2]Orthographic Camera:[/h2]

Switch to the top-down view for an option to use an orthographic camera, useful for creating 2D maps from 3D environments.

[h2]Dice Improvements:[/h2]

Roll various dice types simultaneously and use Alt+Left Click for quick, non-physical dice rolls.

[h2]New Winter-Themed Dice:[/h2]

A free winter-themed dice pack has been added to the DLC options, a gift from the developers to the players.

notes.notes:
[h1]v0.7.10 Small Update[/h1]

[h2]Additions[/h2]
We are excited to announce a new feature to GME. This update gives you the ability to save minis for future use making playing your TTRPGs just a little easier. You'll be able to save the stats of any mini you want and can bring it back into any world you need with those stats carried over.

There are two ways to do this.
1. While searching through minis in the Library you can press Ctrl + Left Click on any mini button to add it to your "Quiver". It will create a new entry for you with blank stats.
2. If you already have a mini down with some stats and you want to save it for later you only need to open the mini radial menu with Right Click. You will see a save icon that will take all of its stats and info and create a new entry in your quiver for you.

Any time you want to bring these minis into your world you can click where the mini button is normally at the bottom of the screen and choose to go to your "Mini Quiver" instead of looking at the normal Library.

[h2]Changes[/h2]
The UI for the main menu was overhauled greatly. The goal is to make something that is much simpler and cleaner for everyone to use. It all functions mostly the same with the exception of a new addition in that being you can select "Simple Map Sizes" when creating worlds. Instead of having to select your X/Y grid size you can pick between some already laid out options. Of course, you can still opt to use custom settings if none of the simple ones are to your liking.

The main menu also had the rendered 3D background removed for now to judge how much it increases performance for those who are just starting up GME for the first time.

Additionally, those of you who like creating maps with the free version of GME have now been given three save slots instead of just one. We hope this lets you take more time to enjoy GME and try out some of the new features!

[h3]Thank You[/h3]
I would like to say thanks to everyone who has supported GME and continues to use it for your TTRPGs we aim to keep polishing what we have until everything works flawlessly!

Lastly, this notebook uses a tag system so you can take plain looking notes and give them some more structure. By giving some text a specific tag you can change the way it looks in the example given below.

There are a total of 16 unique tags to begin playing with. Those include <T> <ST> <H1> <H2> <H3> <B> <I> <BI> <S> <Red> <Green> <Blue> <Yellow> <Purple> <Cyan> <Gray>. No tags will leave the text as default.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/IaEGwI2.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/IaEGwI2.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Spell Book & Attacks Book[/h2]

	Our next new addition is the Spell Book along with the Attacks Book. Similar to how the map notes work you can save some information in these books. Intended for spells and attacks these books are layed out similar in look to the notebook from before but are structured more to favor the 5e spell layout in the PHB. The difference with these books is that they don’t save only to the map and are saved to the engine overall. You will have access to whatever you write down in these pages anywhere you go.

The reason for having two different books is that one was intended for you to save spells to the “Spell Book” and keep the original version of it while the “Attacks Book” will be able to keep copied versions or modified versions on that spell. You don’t even have to save spells here; you could also save melee attacks such as a Halberd. The future plan for these books is to also allow for you to save dice rolls here. That way when you are looking up a spell or an attack you can easily press a button that has your saved dice roll in it.

Please keep in mind that these new note features are experimental still and are likely to change. As people use them and find ways to improve them I will go back and rework the system to improve its usability. After we find a good system to finalize I will then take all of that and rework it into a better file saving system. Right now all the spells/attacks save are unique to the GME user in a file that is not editable outside of GME. I would like to see this system turned into one where you can open the save file outside of GME and add/remove spells as you please. Also, it would be great to see people sharing their spell books with others so everyone can create and grow a big library together.

[url=https://i.imgur.com/vf6BfoW.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/vf6BfoW.png[/img][/url]

[url=https://i.imgur.com/kKwJ6Ra.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/kKwJ6Ra.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Initiative Tracker[/h2]

	This next feature is only for GMs but I hope to update it later so it can be usable by players too. To use this feature you will first need to have minis on the map and give them each a name. After that you can open the initiative window and click the gear icon to start adding turn orders. Give each turn a mini and it will save them to that slot. After your turn order is finished you can then close the gear and begin your initiative. Press the left/right arrows to either go to the next turn or go back a turn. The two windows below the arrows represent which mini/characters turn it currently is as well as who is coming up next. Once you have clicked the right arrow enough times to go through everyone's turn the round number will increase. You can do this an infinite number of times.

All of this info saves to the map whenever you save the map overall. That way you can close down the session and come back to the battle later!

[url=https://i.imgur.com/Szg1bbS.png][img]https://i.imgur.com/Szg1bbS.png[/img][/url]

[h2]Rulers[/h2]

	The last new feature is a much needed set of rulers. By clicking the ruler you can slide out a set of different ruler types to choose from (Line, Sphere and Circle). After choosing the ruler type you want, all you need to do is click anywhere on the map to spawn it in.

Once a ruler is in the world you can grab one of its end nodes to move it around and the line in the center will follow and read out the distance. At any time you can right click one of these nodes to bring up a window to easily delete the ruler once you are done with it.

notes.title: Feature Update: v0.7.4.3
notes.notes:
[h1][b]Hey Everyone![/b][/h1]

This update features our all-new grid overlay system. You can also customize this grid with a number of unique customizations options including color, opacity, and glow. We also introduced Z snapping, which will allow props to be easily placed on top of one another. A few minor and major bugs were addressed, and we made some UI changes to accommodate the new features. 

 
[h3][b]Grid Overlay:[/b][/h3]
You can now apply a grid overlay to your map. This will allow you to easily visualize the map for movement, combat, or other things that require measurement. We also added the option to change the grid color, its opacity, and its glow. 

[h3][b]Top-down Camera:[/b][/h3]
We re-added the top-down camera, which will allow the user to lock their camera at a 90-degree angle to the floor. This will allow you to view your 3d map in 2d and use it more as a battle map like you would see at a classic tabletop session. 

[h3][b]Z Snapping:[/b][/h3]
You now have the ability to toggle Z snapping, which will allow you to more easily stack props on top of each other. This is useful to keep minis on top of bridges, if you want to put some trees on top of rocks, or other occasions when you need to quickly put a prop on top of another. You can turn this option on/off via a button on the top left of the screen. 

[h3][b]UI Changes:[/b][/h3]
We made some UI changes to accommodate the new features added to this patch. The ping button has been moved to the top left of the screen, along with the grid overlay options, camera options, and Z/grid snapping options. 

[h3][b]Bug Fixes:[/b][/h3]
We also did out standard bug fixes and quality of life changes for this update including the removal of the "map loaded" sound, etc.


[b]You may have noticed that the new tile system is not included in this update.[/b] Unfortunately we ran into a few last-minute issues in adding it to the game at this time, nothing too crazy but we want to make sure the tool is more polished before releasing it to the community. These changes will definitely be coming soon, however. Thanks for everyone's understanding! :)

notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=jpZ2FuJreeg;full][/previewyoutube]


[h1][b]Hey Everyone![/b][/h1]

This month we focused on adding many of the systems that are required to play any tabletop RPG including chat features, dice rolling, and damage/healing applications. We also added a few quality-of-life-building tools such as copy/paste, line building, and more. Finally, we took care of a few bugs that were causing issues when building.
 
[h3][b]General & RP Chat:[/b][/h3]
This update introduces a brand new chat window. You can now send messages to the group through the in-game chat feature. This chat is currently divided into two different sections: General and Role Playing. General chat is for out-of-character speaking, comments, questions, or other general use. The role-playing section of the chat will allow you to assign your name however you like and have messages appear as different characters, which is especially useful for a Game Master who role-plays many different characters at once. 

[h3][b]Dice Rolling & Modifiers:[/b][/h3]
Not only does the chat window allow you to send messages between players but it also allows you to roll dice and share the results with the group. You can even choose to include a positive or negative modifier with the roll and have it automatically calculate the total. 

[b]Current dice options include:[/b]
[list]
[*] d2
[*] d4
[*] d6
[*] d8
[*] d10
[*] d12
[*] d20
[/list]
[h3][b]Damage & Healing:[/b][/h3]
You can use the results of the dice rolls to apply damage or healing directly to a mini. When you're finished rolling you can click the red or green icon next to the result and then click any mini. This will automatically apply the roll as damage or healing (depending on which you choose) to the minis health bar. Make sure the "show nameplate" option is checked and that there is HP assigned to the mini.

[h3][b]Mini-movement Distance Measuring:[/b][/h3]
When moving a mini a line will be created from its point of origin. This line will measure the distance the mini has moved, measured in both feet and number of tiles. The tile that the mini was last on will also be highlighted for quick reference. This is just the beginning of a whole set of measuring tools soon to come.

[h3][b]Copy & Paste:[/b][/h3]
Copying and pasting items is now possible. Hover over an object and press ctl+c to copy and a duplicate of that object will appear in your hand, ready to place. The rotation of the object will also be copied with it. This was a much-needed quality of life feature that was finally able to be added to the game.

[h3][b]Line Placement:[/b][/h3]
Speaking of quality of life features, you can now place an entire row of items, minis, and props with the shift key. Hold shift and move your cursor to the desired destination. The game will calculate a straight line between the origin point and your cursor and will place a line of objects on it. This will make placing large walls much easier to manage!

[h3][b]Bug Fixes:[/b][/h3]
There was an issue we fixed where the prop elevation would snap to the floor when placed or moved above an area that doesn't have tiles. We also fixed an issue where props would move up/down very slightly after setting a props elevation with the scroll wheel. If you notice any other bugs you can help us with then please let us know over on our [url=https://discord.gg/F6nnwTrGMV]Discord[/url] server!

notes.title: Multiplayer Update & Future Pricing Model
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We are happy to finally be able to announce the beginning of our multiplayer addition to Game Master Engine! There is a lot to unpack and discuss here so please take the time to read this post to fully understand all of the big changes.


[h1]How Does Multiplayer Work?[/h1]

We are very excited about this addition and we are also equally excited to announce that we will be offering a [b]"Free Edition"[/b] of Game Master Engine along with a [b]"GM Edition"[/b] on the Steam page very soon! Let's talk about how this will work.

We will be restructuring how Game Master Engine will appear on the store page. You should notice very soon that GME will appear to be "Free" with a "GM Edition" DLC. We have done this to make GME more accessible to groups who just want to play their favorite TTRPGs online in a 3D world without having to also drop a ton of cash in the process. The two separate of editions of GME will include the following.

[b]GM Edition[/b]
Owners of this DLC will be able to. 
- Host sessions for their players to join.
- Create unlimited battle and overworld maps.
- Unlock future updates for GM campaign management.
- Unlock future unannounced content packs.

[b]Free Edition[/b]
Owners of this edition will be able to. 
- Join sessions hosted by their GM 
- Create maps in single player with a single save slot.

You may have a couple of questions about all of this so let's take a second to address them here.


[h3]Do I need to buy the GM Edition DLC if I already owned Game Master Engine before this update?[/h3]

No, once Game Master Engine releases the "Free Edition", everyone who has purchased it up until that point will automatically be granted the GM Edition for free.

[h3]Does only the GM need to buy the DLC to host a session?[/h3]

Correct, only a single GM Edition of Game Master Engine needs to be purchased in order to start playing together!


[h3]When will these changes hit the store so my players don't need to purchase GME to play with me?[/h3]

We are currently waiting on Steam to review the DLC package and as soon as it is approved we will make the changes to the store page. There is no exact date currently but it really should be any day now. There will be another announcement once that happens.


[h1]What Has Changed?[/h1]

Game Master Engine likely feels very different from the moment you open the game all the way up to interacting and editing maps. This is due to us taking the last several months to completely rebuild the engine behind it.

This was done to achieve a few things.

[h3]First[/h3]
The previous version of Game Master Engine was bloated and didn't react very well to your inputs and would also take a long time to load maps. Most of this should now be fixed with much smoother loading and object interaction.

[h3]Second[/h3]
We restructured our library of objects including Props, Walls, Effects and Minis. This was done so we could categorize them and present them to you the user in a more organized method. Not only that, the recategorization allows us to add future features like a "Search" bar and a "Favorites" hotbar. Some well needed quality of life features we would like to see added soon.

[h3]Third[/h3]
We added some more content into the game. We now currently have.

- 1,081 Props (978 Fantasy) (103 Sci-Fi)
- 70 Tile Materials
- 44 Walls
- 46 Mini-Figures
- 56 Effects

With much more soon to come!

[h3]Fourth[/h3]
This one comes with a saddened heart, but because of the rebuild of the engine you will notice that any maps you made before v0.7 are no longer compatible with the engine. We truly wish there was a way to avoid this but in order to clean up the coding behind the scenes it was necessary to achieve an overall better engine.

Although, we have kept the old version of Game Master Engine on our website under the download page. This will stay there for you to go back to and use your old maps just incase you don't want to completely lose them. Link immediately below.

https://www.gamemasterengine.com/downloads

Thank you all so much for your love and support so far! We plan to keep working on GME very hard to make sure it takes care of your virtual TTRPG needs.

Sincerely,
The GME Team
